findings.title: Tracked provisioning and host metadata in diagnostic snapshots
evidence: The profile contains one authorized device entry and one public signing certificate.
The system and App Group inventories contain local identifying metadata.
findings.why_it_matters: The files expose host, account and certificate metadata to repository readers.
safe_verification_steps: Inspect plist key names and count matching paths without displaying values.
remediation: Replace raw files with a scrubbed summary and keep authenticated evidence in private storage.
regression_tests: Review staged diagnostic files for private signing inputs and unredacted device or account fields.

findings.title: Explicit detach crosses a reusable BSD device-name boundary
evidence: The teardown validates the exact attachment and media identity.
The native detach command still takes a device name after that validation.
findings.why_it_matters: A platform-side device reuse during the handoff could invalidate the proof of ownership.
safe_verification_steps: Run the existing discovery test with simulated media replacement and verify native busy retry on disposable images.
remediation: Investigate a documented identity-bound detach interface. Keep ordinary detach and pre- and post-operation checks.
regression_tests: Preserve the simulated media-replacement and incomplete-inventory refusal cases.

findings.title: The encrypted backing worker previously acknowledged ordinary fsync
evidence: The worker now requires Darwin F_FULLFSYNC and propagates its errors.
The writable mount checks support before exposing a decrypted image.
findings.why_it_matters: Ordinary fsync can leave writes in a device cache. Stronger flush requests and successful call propagation are prerequisites for the durability test.
safe_verification_steps: Run the protocol fault tests and confirm full-sync requests on disposable backing files.
remediation: Retain the strict worker flush policy and validate native inner-filesystem process interruption.
regression_tests: Inject EINTR, EIO and ENOTSUP and assert the expected status from the worker.
